newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone rebel chief to visit guerrilla base.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebel chief to visit guerrilla base.

text.p: Sierra Leone's rebel leader Foday Sankoh is expected to brief his guerrillas in a jungle base this week on plans to end the country's civil war, government and aid sources said on Monday.
A senior official said the government had approved Sankoh's request to be allowed to travel from Ivory Coast, where he has stayed since leaving his base for peace talks last March.
Sankoh wants to brief his guerrillas on a peace accord he is expected to sign with the government of President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah on ending Sierra Leone's five-year-old civil war.
"Sankoh has asked the government to give him three days in Sierra Leone so he can speak to his men in the country," said the official who asked not to be named.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), which whisked Sankoh by helicopter from his secret jungle camp in March, said it had again been asked to arrange his travel.

"The ICRC is willing to grant the government's request to fly corporal Foday Sankoh into Sierra Leone, but the date has yet to be decided by the government and Sankoh himself," ICRC representative Laurent Fellay told Reuters in Freetown.
Government officials say the government and Sankoh's Revolutionary United Front (RUF) could seal a comprehensive peace accord later this month or in early October.
Kabbah has maintained contacts with Sankoh in Abidjan since peace talks broke off there two months ago over RUF's insistence on the departure of South African mercenaries helping the army.

RUF has not announced any change in its stand but diplomats say they expect Sankoh to eventually soften his position because he has little choice. His guerrillas succeeded in disrupting Sierra Leone's mining economy but they control no major towns or strategic territory to use as bargaining chips.
Both Sankoh and his rag-tag army have confessed to war fatigue. The guerrilla leader has shown no inclination to returning to a jungle life since coming to Abidjan.
Finance Minister Thaimu Bangura told Reuters on Saturday that Sankoh had now dropped a major rebel condition -- that RUF be involved in drawing up the national budget.

The government is anxious to demonstrate clear progress in the peace process ahead of a donors meeting in Geneva on Tuesday and Wednesday. Sierra Leone will be seeking a $1 billion aid package for post-war rehabilitation and reconstruction.

"International donor funding of the rehabilitation and reconstruction of the country is predicated on the negotiations," Bengura said. "News of this (budget) breakthrough will certainly encourage the donors to help."
